title: Niche topics people miss
objectives: Explain equalisation reserve, ELSS reinvestment lock-ins, daily IDCW, unclaimed IDCW and NRI TDS.
Say where IDCW and TDS appear in the CAS and the tax return.
body_md:
These are the IDCW details that most often catch out distributors.

| Topic | What it is | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Equalisation reserve | Part of the price paid by new investors that the scheme sets aside, so existing gains aren't diluted; it can form part of the distributable surplus | This is how a new investor's own money can come back to them as "income" |
| ELSS with IDCW reinvestment | Each reinvested unit is a fresh purchase with its own 3-year lock-in | Units unlock at different dates; harder to track and redeem |
| Daily or weekly IDCW in liquid funds | Frequent small payouts, often reinvested | Each one is taxable and adds to paperwork; growth is usually simpler |
| "Monthly income" hybrid funds | Funds marketed for regular payouts | Payouts still depend on surplus; check equity exposure and the riskometer |
| Unclaimed IDCW | Payouts that fail because of an old or closed bank account | Keep bank details updated; unclaimed amounts need a claim process with the AMC |
| NRI investors | TDS on IDCW for NRIs is at higher rates than for residents | Check the current rate and any tax-treaty relief with the client's CA |
| TDS declarations | Eligible resident investors with income below the taxable limit can submit declarations so that TDS isn't deducted | Useful for low-income retirees taking IDCW |
| Reporting in the tax return | IDCW must be reported as income even after TDS | Clients often miss this; give them the yearly IDCW statement |
| IDCW in the CAS | The CAS and AMC statements show IDCW paid and TDS deducted | Use them in the annual review and at tax time |

> **Investor takeaway:** Ask each new joiner to show, using the NAV table, why buying just before a record date doesn't make money, and to explain it to a partner in under a minute.
example: New investor's purchase price partly set aside as equalisation reserve can later return to them as “income” — the clearest proof that IDCW can be own money back.
say: IDCW must be reported as income even after TDS.
Keep bank details updated, or payouts go unclaimed.
never: Unclaimed IDCW is lost forever with no claim process.
NRI TDS on IDCW is lower than for residents.
